coherence.reasons: Both follow the same sound logic: the US is worth entering, Amazon fits the limits, retail breaks them, ad cost is the swing factor, then gates. X's summary line and section title say Amazon-led "meets the board's cash, payback and margin limits", yet its next section shows payback fails at the 32% benchmark and only just holds at the pilot's 28%. The qualification is there, but the hierarchy states a pass first and then undercuts it. Y's scorecard marks payback "At risk" from the start, and its three pillars (worth entering, only Amazon fits, what the board has to accept) carry that through to the decisions requested. Y's governing thought also covers all three options, including deferring Japan. X is well structured and its gates link back to the analysis, so the difference is small.

judgment.reasons: Both reach the key's preferred recommendation (Amazon-led with gates, retail only above 20% awareness, Japan weighed as the alternative) and both test the options against the board's own constraints. Y is more explicit about the trade-offs the board must accept: no route reaches $40M within the limits, so reset it as a 2031–32 milestone; accept that 2030 payback is at risk; authorise a $4M envelope. It also adds a second retail gate ($20M Amazon sales at ACoS of 30% or less) and a 300-door test sized to margin headroom. X treats the $40M gap as "one of timing" and flags the reading for the board, which is softer than presenting it as a choice. X is stronger in two places: its ACoS gate sits at the 28.6% break-even, whereas Y's review trigger only fires above 32% for two quarters, leaving a band where payback is already missed without a review. X also names Japan as the fallback if ACoS stays above break-even. These roughly offset; Y's clearer statement of the ambition-versus-constraints trade gives it a small edge.

evidence.reasons: The two models agree with each other and with the key on every required figure: $4.73 and $7.55 per unit, −$20.8M peak for B, 4.5% group margin in 2027, break-even ACoS of 28.6%, and the ACoS and tariff grid. Both set aside the $5.2B figure, both check 4.5 units per door against the awareness bands and the 4.0 cut-off, and both note that two of three Amazon-first peers stalled. X handles the 0.71 correlation more thoroughly (reverse cause, common cause, and a quantified test that the halo's $3.98M would not cover $31.6M of retail cost) and adds the 19 units per door break-even. Y scrutinises the pilot better: it notes monthly growth slowed from 16–17% to 8–9% and that the 2027 plan needs 1.8 times the June run-rate. X instead claims the growth is "a sign of word of mouth" and that the pilot "understates" a full range, neither of which the pack supports. Y also gives the break-even under a tariff rise (26.9%), tests ACoS up to 38%, and runs retail on realistic inputs (−$31M). Y's inference that the 52% price finding favours the $24 Amazon price is a mild stretch, and its 2032 payback rests on an illustrative extension, though it says so. X's 2032 extrapolation at 29% growth is less conservative than Y's 25%. Close overall, with Y slightly more careful about optimistic assumptions.

revision.reasons: Both keep the CEO's Amazon-first hypothesis with conditions, as the evidence warrants, and both set out explicit changes from the CEO's draft. X makes three: retail trigger raised from 15% to 20% awareness, ACoS gated at 28.6% rather than assumed to fall to 25%, and a targeted door test instead of a specialty-retail rollout from 2029. Y raises awareness to 20%, lifts the Amazon scale gate from $10M to $20M at ACoS of 30% or less, proposes a 300-door test, and moves timing to 2030 at the earliest. Y also explicitly resets the $40M ambition, which the key treats as part of the right handling. X corrects the CEO's ACoS assumption more sharply but drops the Amazon-sales trigger without replacing it and leaves the ambition as a timing note. Both revisions are grounded in the pack; Y's is marginally more complete.

overall.reasons: Both are strong, numerically accurate documents that reach the defensible recommendation and avoid the main traps. Y serves the board slightly better because it turns the analysis into the choices the board actually has to make: approve Amazon-led with a $4M envelope, accept that 2030 payback is at risk, and reset $40M to 2031–32 because no route reaches it within the limits. It is also more sceptical of the pilot and stress-tests more widely. X has the deeper treatment of the correlation memo and a tighter ACoS gate at break-even with a Japan fallback, but its headline that Amazon "meets" the payback limit and its softer handling of the ambition gap make the central tension less clear. Y's loose 32% review trigger is its main weakness.
